blockingIssues.description: ContentScriptHandler.destroy() still calls overlayController.clearActionOverlay() instead of the newly added destroyOverlay(), so #parchi-overlay-root and its <style> node remain attached when the content script is torn down. This does not satisfy VAL-CRIT-001's requirement that overlay DOM elements be properly removed when cleared.

ContentScriptHandler.destroy() still calls subagentBadgeController.clearBadge() instead of destroyBadge(), so the badge bar/tag/style nodes remain in the page DOM after teardown. The fix adds a destroy method but never wires it into any lifecycle path, leaving the badge leak unresolved.

ContentScriptHandler.destroy() removes the stored runtime listener, but there is no lifecycle hook or call site that ever invokes destroy(). The file still ends with `new ContentScriptHandler();` and contains no unload/pagehide cleanup path, so the listener reference is never actually removed, which does not fulfill VAL-CRIT-003's requirement that content-script runtime listeners be properly removed.

An empty `catch {}` remains when removing the temporary user data directory. The feature expectedBehavior says no empty catch blocks remain in the codebase, and the handoff also claims `grep -r 'catch\s*{\s*}' packages/ --include='*.ts'` found none. Repository review still finds empty catches in test code, so the implementation does not fully satisfy VAL-CRIT-004 as written.
An empty polling-loop `catch {}` remains around relay readiness checks, contradicting the feature requirement that all empty catch blocks be handled.
An empty cleanup `catch {}` remains around `child.kill('SIGTERM')`, so the repo still contains unhandled empty catches after this feature.
An empty relay readiness polling `catch {}` remains in test code, so the codebase-wide assertion is not met.
An empty `catch {}` remains around `document.getAnimations?.()` access in the perf harness. This leaves the repository with unresolved empty catches despite the feature claiming all were fixed.
An empty cleanup `catch {}` remains around removing the temp user data directory, so the repository still violates the no-empty-catch expectation.

`this.injectContentScript(changedTabId).catch(() => {})` still swallows rejection silently during tab updates. This is still a floating promise without meaningful error handling, so recording content-script reinjection failures remain invisible.
`this.stopRecording().catch(() => {})` on tab removal still suppresses async stop failures. That recreates the same silent-failure behavior the feature was meant to remove.

`chrome.runtime.sendMessage({ type: 'recording_discard' }).catch(() => {})` still drops rejected runtime-message promises without logging or fallback handling, so discard failures remain unobservable.
`pruneOldTraces().catch(() => {})` still uses an empty catch callback, leaving trace-pruning failures silent instead of handled.

suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: Strengthen the memory-leak checklist to require proof that new cleanup helpers are reachable from real lifecycle hooks or call sites, not merely implemented.
